hypothesis: Genuine quantum measurement randomness would produce meaningfully different entropy characteristics than a standard PRNG, and I wanted to see that difference on real hardware instead of taking it on faith from a textbook.
outcome: The entropy difference was real but small at the scale I could test. The actual lesson was operational, not theoretical: queue times shared on quantum hardware make 'real-time' quantum randomness impractical for anything latency-sensitive, which is a constraint no algorithms course mentions.
